reviews.notes: Opening divine qualities: fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge, charity, self-restraint, sacrifice, study, austerity, and uprightness; ends cleanly at 'Uprightness,'.
Continuation of divine qualities: harmlessness, truth, freedom from wrath, renunciation, peace, non-slander, compassion, uncovetousness, gentleness, modesty, steadiness; ends at 'grave,'.

Concluding divine qualities: vigour/radiance, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, freedom from malice and excessive pride, characterizing one born to divine destiny; starts at 'with manhood nobly mixed'.
Demonic qualities: hypocrisy, pride, arrogance, wrath, harshness, and ignorance, belonging to one born of demonic destiny; includes footnote 32.
Divine endowment leads to liberation, demonic to bondage; Krishna reassures Arjuna that he is born with divine qualities.
Two orders of created beings in this world: the divine and the demonic; divine described at length, hear now of the demonic.
Demonic persons know neither right action nor renunciation; neither purity, right conduct, nor truth is found in them.
They say the world is without truth, without moral basis, without a Lord, brought about by sexual union alone, caused only by lust.
Holding this view, these ruined souls of small intellect and fierce deeds emerge as enemies of the world for its destruction.
Surrendering to insatiable desires, full of hypocrisy, pride, and arrogance, holding false notions through delusion, they act with unholy vows; ends cleanly at 'sinful course,'.
Beset with boundless anxieties ending only in death, regarding sensual enjoyment as the highest goal, convinced that this is all; starts cleanly at 'they trust this lie'.
Bound by hundreds of ties of hope, devoted to lust and anger, they strive by unjust means to accumulate wealth for sense gratification.
Inner monologue of the demonic: 'This has been gained by me today; this desire I shall obtain; this wealth is mine, and this also shall be mine in future'.
Demonic boasting: 'That enemy has been slain by me, and others also I shall slay; I am the lord, I enjoy, I am successful, powerful, and happy'.
Demonic self-glorification: 'I am wealthy and well-born; who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, give alms, and rejoice', deluded by ignorance; ends at 'ignorance;'.
Bewildered by numerous thoughts, entangled in the mesh of delusion, addicted to gratification of lust, they fall into foul Naraka; starts at 'and so they fall--'.
Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform ostentatious sacrifices in name only, disregarding scriptural injunctions.
Given over to egotism, power, insolence, lust, and wrath, these malicious people hate Me dwelling in their own bodies and those of others; ends at 'my foemen are,'.
Those who hate, cruel, evil, lowest of men—I cast them perpetually into demonic wombs in the cycle of samsara; ends at 'devilish womb,'.
Fallen into demonic wombs, deluded birth after birth, failing to reach Me, they sink to the lowest degradation; starts at 'whence--birth by birth--'.
Threefold is the gate of hell leading to self-ruin: lust, anger, and greed; therefore let a man renounce these three.
The man who is released from these three gates of darkness acts for his own welfare and thereby reaches the supreme goal.
Verified source omission. The source omits canonical 16.23 on disregarding scriptural rules; Arnold terminates the chapter rendering after 16.22 with footnote 33.

Verified source omission. The source omits canonical 16.24 on scripture as the standard of action; footnote 33 claims omission of 'ten concluding shlokas' (a source marker anomaly, as standard canon has 24 verses).

chapterFindings: Translator footnote 33 asserts the omission of 'the ten concluding shlokas, with Mr Davis', whereas standard canonical Chapter 16 has 24 verses total, leaving exactly two omitted shlokas (16.23–16.24); this discrepancy is a historical source anomaly correctly preserved.
The divine virtues catalog in 16.1–16.3 is split with exceptional accuracy across line boundaries (line 6 at 'Uprightness,' and line 13 at 'manhood nobly mixed').
Careful segmentation of demonic psychological profiles across verses 16.10–16.11, 16.15–16.16, and 16.19–16.20 accurately reflects the Sanskrit syntactic units.
